findings.summary: Portrait captions are rendered as figcaption elements without a figure parent.
findings.consequence: The markup is invalid and assistive technology/browser semantics do not associate the editorial caption with the portrait image as a figure caption; tests currently assert only that a figcaption exists, not that it is correctly attached to the image.
findings.evidence: The ordinary branch opens a plain div at line 122, renders the img on lines 123-127, then renders RenderableHtmlContent as figcaption at line 130 via the component call starting on line 128. The Dramawebben branch repeats the same pattern: a plain div at line 206 contains img lines 207-211 and RenderableHtmlContent as figcaption starting line 212. RenderableHtmlContent renders props.as directly, so these are physical figcaption elements under divs.
findings.recommendation: Change each portrait wrapper that contains an image and caption from div to figure, preserving the existing classes on the figure; keep figcaption as the first or last child of that figure and add an SSR or component test that asserts `.portrait_container figure > img + figcaption`.
